about: Visible Fear is a close-up of Peter Parker (Tobey Maguire) in the red homemade mask he wears for the cage wrestling match in Spider-Man (2002). He is looking up from the mat with huge, darting eyes, the only part of his face the mask leaves exposed, and a yellow subtitle at the bottom reads "Visible fear", written like a closed-caption sound description. The joke is that the caption is completely unnecessary: his eyes already say everything. People use it as their own face at the exact moment they realise something is about to go wrong, whether it is a deploy, a pop quiz or a group project.
origin: The frame comes from the wrestling sequence in Sam Raimi's Spider-Man (2002), when the newly powered Peter enters an underground cage match against Bonesaw McGraw. The "Visible fear" subtitle was added in a screenshot that spread as a stand-alone reaction image.
usage:
Your text goes in the lone box across the top. Write the trigger, usually starting with "when": the message, sound or announcement that causes the panic. The built-in "Visible fear" subtitle already delivers the punchline, so your line only has to set up the threat.

It works best for small, specific warnings that mean big trouble: a calendar invite titled "quick chat", a teacher saying "clear your desks", a mechanic going quiet. The calmer and more ordinary the wording of the setup, the funnier the terrified eyes look.
ideas: when the intern says "i optimized the database"
when the teacher says "clear your desks"
when your boss books a 15 min call called "quick chat"
when the opposing team brings in a 6'8" sub
when your mom says "we need to talk" and uses your full name
when the game says "checkpoint reached" right before a boss door
